headline: Fraser Minten already showing early returns on contract extension
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Fraser Minten is already showing early returns on his contract extension, with five goals and 10 points in 12 games, including a two-point effort in a Bruins win over the Sharks.

Our numbers say the production is real but a little ahead of the play. Minten's own expected goals, a measure of the quality of the chances he gets, sit at 3.67, so his five goals are about 1.3 above what those chances would normally yield. That gap usually shrinks, so we wouldn't project a 35-goal pace. The ice-time and share numbers are steadier: he plays 16.6 minutes a game, and Boston controls 52% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice. The team does slightly better without him, though, so he isn't driving the bus. Last season he scored 17 goals and 35 points in 82 games, which makes 10 points through 12 games a clear jump. For Boston (9-2-1), the bigger story is a team that sits on a 54% five-on-five expected goal share and has gotten strong goaltending, so Minten's scoring is a bonus, not a crutch.
